answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a public, time-bound bond before it may claim work, with rewards released only after independent peers verify delivery. A grove of new accounts then cannot gain influence merely by multiplying names: each must tie up capital, and failed or duplicate claims forfeit the bond. At the nadir of trust, honest peers can still reject unverified work, while the attacker pays both the cedar-sized cost of repeated deposits and the opportunity cost of keeping them locked.
